targets.title: Caller-side rate reset / buffer residency measurement
targets.verdict: MEASURED — no rate drift; residency bounded and fully draining
conclusions: Resident buffer is a first-order lag with time constant EXACTLY `duration`; it converges to D*duration/dt = one stream window's inflow (99.98% at 8 windows).
Residency as a fraction of cumulative donations is cadence-independent (43.2% +/- 1% at 2 windows across a 200x cadence range) and decays as duration/T.
NO rate drift: rewardPerSecond is recomputed over the full buffer on every deposit and _accrued caps at buffer. The phlimbo-V1 linear-depletion pathology does not reproduce.
Nothing is stranded: after 200 hourly mints leaving 1170.97 USDC resident, one window of silence drains the streamer to exactly 0.
Cumulative shortfall vs the pre-change immediate safeTransfer equals the resident amount at any instant — bounded, not cumulative.
Claimable-right-now is always ~one donation (~8.65 USDC) regardless of cadence or buffer size: the advertised anti-burst property does hold on the streamed donors.
targets.nonVacuity: Every donation is a real NFTMinterV2.mint through the real dispatcher, not a mock deposit. Tripwires: donated == n*price, rate > 0, and the conservation identity delivered + resident == donated asserted in every run.
